summary.text: A 32-year-old Mongolian primigravida with unremarkable medical and family histories had onset of proteinuria at 38 weeks gestation and significant proteinuria at 39 weeks gestation with suspected pre-eclampsia, was admitted to a different facility, and had a cesarean section at 40 weeks. Massive intraoperative and postoperative bleeding occurred, with a fluid infusion given, and hypertension is described both after the cesarean section and before delivery (source conflict).

She was transferred for uncontrollable bleeding. On admission she had drowsiness, conjunctival pallor, severe anemia, leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, impaired renal function, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia and coagulopathy diagnosed as DIC; she received 11 units of red blood cells, 16 units of fresh frozen plasma and 20 units of platelets. Contrast CT showed uterine contrast extravasation and a non-enhancing renal cortex with enhancing medulla (reverse rim sign consistent with RCN).

An endovascular intervention achieved hemostasis. She remained anuric and CHDF was started in the ICU. She developed persistent thrombocytopenia, elevated liver enzymes and decreased haptoglobin, diagnosed as HELLP syndrome, and other causes of thrombotic microangiopathy were investigated (STEC-HUS and TTP ruled out, no genetic mutations on atypical HUS testing). Nicardipine infusion and a 2-day dexamethasone course were given and liver enzymes and thrombocytopenia gradually improved.

She left the ICU on the 11th day, moving from CHDF to intermittent hemodialysis. Renal biopsy on the 23rd day showed coagulative necrosis of glomeruli and tubules in the outer cortex with glomerular paralysis and sparing of the deeper cortex, consistent with renal cortical necrosis, with no glomerulonephritis. Hemodialysis was discontinued on the 22nd day after admission and resumed on the 35th day; she chose peritoneal dialysis, began it on the 48th day and was discharged on the 53rd day.

Dialysis was discontinued about 6 months after discharge according to the case narrative (about 6 months post-onset in the discussion, source conflict) with serum creatinine 4.39 mg/dL. Four years post-discharge she remains free of renal replacement therapy with serum creatinine 2.67 mg/dL while receiving treatment for metabolic acidosis and renal anemia. The Figure 4 caption names darbepoetin α in the post-discharge course.
